contract.note: Reading AGI as broadly accepted or independently verified human-level general intelligence is the ordinary reading. Treating it as confirmable only by a decisive field-wide conclusion is fair for an open-ended forecast. The undefined term AGI drives the result.

A single developer self-report does not meet that bar, so the claim is unresolved.

contract.note: Higher task success counts, but speed and new input formats do not. This tracks the speaker's own exceptions. Counting reasoning models as generative AI is ordinary. The early-contradiction rule is fair.

evidence.note: An independent evaluation, October 2024. o1 reached 97.8% on Blocksworld and 52.8% on the obfuscated version, where prior LLMs scored a few percent. That is a substantial gain on a comparable substantive task beyond the July 2024 baseline.

An independent ARC Prize measurement, September 2024. o1-preview roughly matched Claude 3.5 Sonnet, released before the baseline, on ARC-AGI. This limits how broad the gain is but does not negate the planning result.

reviews.rationale: A dated, independent public evaluation (October 2024) showed o1 far exceeding earlier LLMs on PlanBench, including the obfuscated variants. The gain is in accuracy, not speed or new inputs, which meets the early-contradiction rule. The ARC result shows the gain is not universal but does not undo the substantial improvement.
